title: RideLink Long-Distance Travel and Lodging Allowance Schedule
content:
The Reimbursement Unit's travel schedule for Non-Emergency Medical Transportation lists, by RideLink level of service, the one-way distance above which a trip is long distance, the advance notice a long-distance request needs, whether out-of-state trips need plan approval, and the distance and allowances for lodging and meals.

| Level | Standard one-way limit (miles; above this a trip is long distance) | Long-distance request lead time (business days before the appointment) | Out-of-state trip needs plan approval | Lodging threshold: lodging and meals from (one-way miles) | Standard nightly lodging allowance (USD) | Standard daily meals allowance (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RideLink Transit Pass | 0 | 0 | Yes | 0 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| RideLink Mileage Reimbursement | 50 | 5 | Yes | 120 | 85.00 | 25.00 |
| RideLink Ambulatory Sedan | 50 | 5 | Yes | 120 | 85.00 | 25.00 |
| RideLink Door-to-Door Assist | 50 | 5 | Yes | 120 | 85.00 | 25.00 |
| RideLink Wheelchair Van | 75 | 5 | Yes | 120 | 85.00 | 25.00 |
| RideLink Stretcher Van | 75 | 5 | Yes | 120 | 85.00 | 25.00 |

Notes to the schedule:

1. The standard one-way limit is exceeded only by a trip whose one-way miles are above the figure; a trip of exactly 50 miles on RideLink Ambulatory Sedan, or exactly 75 miles on RideLink Wheelchair Van, is within the limit.
2. The lodging threshold is met at or above the figure: 120 one-way miles meets it, 119 does not.
3. The nightly lodging allowance is stated per lodging night and the daily meals allowance per travel day.
4. RideLink Transit Pass lists 0 for every distance and allowance column.

*Hypothetical reading:* a RideLink Door-to-Door Assist trip of 130 one-way miles is above the 50-mile standard limit and at or above the 120-mile lodging threshold; a RideLink Wheelchair Van trip of 70 one-way miles is within that level's 75-mile standard limit.
